subtopics.title: Kinematics of a particle moving in a straight line
Dynamics of a particle moving in a straight line or plane

command_words.Show that: Prove a given result; every step must be shown (answer given).
command_words.Hence: Use the previous result to reach the answer.
command_words.Hence or otherwise: Using the previous result is expected, but any valid method earns the marks.
command_words.Find: Work out; method marks need working.
command_words.Calculate: Work out from given facts; show working.
command_words.Sketch: Draw the shape with key features labelled (intercepts, asymptotes, turning points), not to scale.
command_words.Exact: Give the answer in surd, fraction, pi or ln form, not a decimal.
command_words.Verify: Show that given values satisfy the statement.
command_words.Interpret: Explain the meaning of a result in the context of the question.

kcs.title: Mechanics modelling assumptions
kcs.statement: The basic ideas of mathematical modelling as applied in Mechanics.
kcs.raw: The basic ideas of mathematical modelling as applied in Mechanics.
kcs.guidance: Students should be familiar with the terms: particle, lamina, rigid body, rod (light, uniform, non-uniform), inextensible string, smooth and rough surface, light smooth pulley, bead, wire, peg. Students should be familiar with the assumptions made in using these models.

kcs.title: Magnitude, direction and resultant vectors
kcs.statement: Magnitude and direction of a vector. Resultant of vectors may also be required.
kcs.raw: Magnitude and direction of a vector. Resultant of vectors may also be required.
kcs.guidance: Students may be required to resolve a vector into two components or use a vector diagram. Questions may be set involving the unit vectors $\mathbf{i}$ and $\mathbf{j}$.

kcs.title: Vectors for displacement, velocity, force
kcs.statement: Application of vectors to displacements, velocities, accelerations and forces in a plane.
kcs.raw: Application of vectors to displacements, velocities, accelerations and forces in a plane.
kcs.guidance: Use of $\text{velocity} = \dfrac{\text{change of displacement}}{\text{time}}$ in the case of constant velocity, and of $\text{acceleration} = \dfrac{\text{change of velocity}}{\text{time}}$ in the case of constant acceleration, will be required.

kcs.title: Constant acceleration in a straight line
kcs.statement: Motion in a straight line with constant acceleration.
kcs.raw: Motion in a straight line with constant acceleration.
kcs.guidance: Graphical solutions may be required, including displacement-time, velocity-time, speed-time and acceleration-time graphs. Knowledge and use of formulae for constant acceleration will be required.

kcs.title: Newton's laws of motion
kcs.statement: The concept of a force. Newton's laws of motion.
kcs.raw: The concept of a force. Newton’s laws of motion.
kcs.guidance: Simple problems involving constant acceleration in scalar form or as a vector of the form $a\mathbf{i} + b\mathbf{j}$.

kcs.title: Connected particles and inclined planes
kcs.statement: Simple applications including the motion of two connected particles.
kcs.raw: Simple applications including the motion of two connected particles.
kcs.guidance: Problems may include: (i) the motion of two connected particles moving in a straight line or under gravity when the forces on each particle are constant; problems involving smooth fixed pulleys and/or pegs may be set; (ii) motion under a force which changes from one fixed value to another, e.g. a particle hitting the ground; (iii) motion directly up or down a smooth or rough inclined plane.

kcs.title: Momentum, impulse and collisions
kcs.statement: Momentum and impulse. The impulse-momentum principle. The principle of conservation of momentum applied to two particles colliding directly.
kcs.raw: Momentum and impulse. The impulse-momentum principle. The principle of conservation of momentum applied to two particles colliding directly.
kcs.guidance: Knowledge of Newton's law of restitution is not required. Problems will be confined to those of a one-dimensional nature.

kcs.title: Coefficient of friction in motion
kcs.guidance: An understanding of $F = \mu R$ when a particle is moving.

kcs.title: Resolving forces as vectors
kcs.statement: Forces treated as vectors. Resolution of forces.
kcs.raw: Forces treated as vectors. Resolution of forces.

kcs.title: Equilibrium of a particle
kcs.statement: Equilibrium of a particle under coplanar forces. Weight, normal reaction, tension and thrust, friction.
kcs.raw: Equilibrium of a particle under coplanar forces. Weight, normal reaction, tension and thrust, friction.
kcs.guidance: Only simple cases of the application of the conditions for equilibrium to uncomplicated systems will be required.

kcs.title: Friction in equilibrium
kcs.guidance: An understanding of $F \le \mu R$ in a situation of equilibrium.

kcs.title: Moments and equilibrium of a body
kcs.guidance: Simple problems involving coplanar parallel forces acting on a body and conditions for equilibrium in such situations.
